content.comment_body: Hello everyone, In [product_name] display using an analog amplifier, I'm able to show temperature readings with decimal places. For example, converting 2563 to 25.63. Is this possible with [product_name] Web Editor? I haven't figured out how to do this yet. I came across a post from two years ago stating that it wasn't possible, but I'm hoping there has been an update to address this. If not, are there alternative methods—perhaps using HTML? Any advice is welcome. Thank you!

It seems you may have misinterpreted something in your research. With the current version of [product_name] Web Editor, this functionality isn't available. If you're comfortable with HTML5, you could manually edit the project files afterwards. Details on this can be found in the manual for [product_name] Web Editor.
Thank you for clarifying. Could you specify what you meant by saying I misunderstood something? English isn't my first language, so sometimes I miss details.

Hello everyone, I have another related question: is it possible to modify HTML to affect the display of the analog bar, in addition to the analog value? I'm attempting to represent the temperature as a float value using both an analog bar and a numerical display. Thanks for any guidance!

It's essentially the same issue, since [product_name] only manages integers, not floats, and the same applies to [product_name] Web Editor. I'm not sure if it's possible with HTML5. Your question suggests you may not be very familiar with HTML5 yet.
Okay, I'll keep following the steps that other users suggested in a previous post from two years ago. Clearly, I'm just getting started with HTML, while you have much more experience.

The analog bar graph does not require values specifically, so you can turn off scaling values in [product_name] Web Editor. You can then create your own scaling using texts such as 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, and so on, in place of the default scale (10, 20, 30, etc.). This requires extra work but it's achievable. For the other values, I've suggested a way that beginners can also use. I believe you’re referring to the [document] with comments explaining how to identify and adjust these values. There could also be a simple method for manipulating analog bars, though I haven't tested it yet, since you can resolve it in [product_name] Web Editor as described above.
It would be great if the most recent [product_name] Web Editor version allowed configuration of decimal points for analog values.

We all hope future software updates make things easier. Here's a small workaround I discovered for manipulating analog bars, though I haven't tested it in [product_name]. If you have an analog bar with scaling, you can adjust the values as text in the main.html file. The provided example manipulates the scaling from 0...100 to 0.0°C...10.0°C. You can load the modified file with [product_name] Web Editor and observe the outcome. Just don't revert the scaling in [product_name] Web Editor after making the changes. See attached images for a visual, and attached text files for HTML snippets before and after modification—it's straightforward to locate these sections.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are unable to display analog values with decimals (floats) in [product_name] Web Editor due to limitations in both the software and associated hardware, which only support integers. Users have attempted workarounds such as manually editing HTML files, but find these solutions technically challenging and inefficient. There is a strong desire among users for a future version of the software that natively supports floating-point representation and more user-friendly configuration options.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] Web Editor to allow analog values to be displayed with decimal points and to offer straightforward configuration for displaying floating-point analog readouts, like temperature, in both analog bars and numerical displays.
